task.title: Study Forensics: Virtual tutoring boosts reading skills
task.prompt: A randomized controlled trial tested a virtual reading tutoring program in a rural school district. The program paired live online tutors with small groups of struggling elementary students for ten-week sessions. Students who completed around forty tutoring sessions gained roughly two additional months of reading progress compared with peers in the control condition. Even those attending fewer sessions showed modest gains. Researchers emphasised that consistent participation was critical and highlighted that the program delivered results at a lower cost than typical high-dose tutoring.
task.context:
A well-designed educational RCT with cautious language and clear limitations.
The agent should recognise this as solid without overflagging.
task.reference_solution: The summary describes a rigorously designed trial of a virtual tutoring program. It reports improved reading outcomes and notes cost effectiveness and the importance of consistent participation without overstating broader impacts.

functional_descriptions: the study uses random assignment, supporting causal claims
authors hedge claims appropriately and note conditions for success

common_errors: hallucinating major flaws in a solid study
treating modest effects as evidence of overclaim
task.diagnostic_focus: Can the agent recognise a well-designed educational RCT without overflagging?
task.gold_summary: The summary describes a rigorously designed trial of a virtual tutoring program. It reports improved reading outcomes and notes cost effectiveness and the importance of consistent participation without overstating broader impacts.

gold_evidence_spans.span: Students who completed around forty tutoring sessions gained roughly two additional months of reading progress compared with peers in the control condition
gold_evidence_spans.why_it_matters: Shows that the primary claim is directly supported by measured outcomes in the trial.

gold_evidence_spans.span: Researchers emphasised that consistent participation was critical and highlighted that the program delivered results at a lower cost than typical high-dose tutoring
gold_evidence_spans.why_it_matters: Demonstrates cautious language and avoids overgeneralization by noting conditions for success.

task.gold_justification:
A randomized controlled trial with clear outcome measures supports the claims.
The summary uses cautious language ("gained roughly two additional months",
"consistency is critical") and does not generalise beyond the study population.
There is no obvious mechanism-evidence mismatch or causal overreach.
task.curator_notes:
Clean solid case from education domain. Tests whether agents avoid flagging
non-problems in a well-conducted RCT with measured language. Good calibration
anchor alongside the existing health-focused solid cases (001, 004).
